A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SDCI and conditional summary graphs, with matching retained experiments and illustrations. All 23 pages of v2 and 25 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V2 reports original linear-system, particle-simulation and NBA forecasting experiments, including graph accuracy, reconstruction error and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V3 reports original particle, simulated gene regulatory network and NBA experiments, including graph identification, state estimation and forecasting results.

M1.justification: V3 introduces hidden recurrent-state inference using a state-transition model, a bidirectional GNN-RNN posterior and a state KL term; v2 supplied states in its collision experiment. V3 also adds recurrent-case edge attention, directly parameterized fixed-graph inference, GRN node embeddings and a revised discrete gradient estimator (Section 3.3; Appendix B.3).

E1.justification: V3 adds DynGen gene regulatory network discovery and spring-plus-magnetic particle interactions, and evaluates recurrent states without supplying them. The linear-system experiments disappear entirely. NBA forecasting remains, but the explicit Toronto-to-Boston transfer scenario is removed; observed-state spring coverage survives in Appendix E.1.

E2.justification: The particle comparison changes from ACD/CD-NOD to ACD/Rhino/Neural Granger Causality. NBA adds Chen et al.'s NRI comparator, called NRI-NPM in the main text and NRI-MPM in Appendix B.4. GRN Table 1 additionally evaluates Regime-PCMCI; TdCM and SAEM disappear with the linear experiments. ACD's 2020-to-2022 citation update denotes the same comparator.

E3.justification: The stated spring training/test counts change from 50,000/10,000, with 200 tests for selected baselines, to 10,000/100. Revised particle experiments introduce fixed-graph controls, micro/macro F1 scoring, different training budgets and batch sizes, and annealed rather than fixed state temperatures. GRN evaluation adds AUROC. These reported settings do not establish that retained appendix figures were rerun.

E4.justification: V3 adds fixed-versus-variable graph controls that distinguish structure recovery from state-estimation difficulty, compares state-information variants on GRNs, and analyzes extracted NBA interaction graphs. V2's fixed-decoder linear ablations, linear failure examples and NBA data-efficiency/transfer tests are removed. The observed-state spring sensitivity, data-efficiency and generalization analyses are retained as Figure 14.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence levels or significance tests. Spring error-bar reporting remains, including the unchanged analysis moved from v2 Figure 4 to v3 Figure 14. The disappearing plus/minus tables accompany removed experiments rather than a documented change in uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: V2's linear and supplied-state collision results are removed, while v3 adds fixed/variable particle results and GRN scores. V3 Table 1 reports 0.936 AUROC and 0.347 F1 for SDCI-determined, versus Rhino's 0.933 and 0.081. NBA curves also change: v3 shows only a slight hidden-state advantage over ACD. Revised settings prevent treating these as matched cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: V2's observed-state full-time and conditional-summary-graph proofs are replaced by a latent-state partial-identifiability framework. V3 introduces Gaussian switching-model and uniqueness assumptions, permutation-based definitions, Theorem 4.3, Theorems A.6–A.7 and Corollary A.8 for structures and edge labels. Appendices B.1–B.2 also add ELBO and state-marginalization derivations.

C1.justification: V2 presents hidden-state discovery as empirically supported while limiting its guarantees to observed states. V3 makes structural identifiability under determined and recurrent latent states a central contribution. Its abstract and conclusion replace the linear-system emphasis with GRN discovery and biological applicability, and extend the NBA comparison claim to NRI.

C2.justification: V3 distinguishes structural identifiability from unresolved state-distribution identification, adds practical uncertainty about choosing K, and expands the estimator-consistency discussion. It explains recurrent-inference difficulties and weak benefits from supplied GRN states through gradual gene deactivation. NBA interpretation additionally emphasizes interaction sparsity and reduced error accumulation through the no-edge mechanism.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C substantially expand architecture, optimization, baseline-tuning and simulation documentation, including recurrent encoder layers and DynGen generation. NBA-specific training and sparsity settings are newly disclosed rather than establishing changes to previously specified settings. Linear-generator and fixed-decoder instructions disappear. PyTorch, RTX 2080 Ti hardware and the NBA data-access reference remain.

R1.justification: V3 substantially reframes the work around switching-model and latent-regime identifiability, adding comparisons with Balsells-Rodas et al. (2024), Varambally et al. (2024) and Song et al. (2024). It also develops biological positioning through DynGen and GRN literature. These changes exceed citation updates or relocation of related work.

P1.justification: The introduction, method exposition and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. V3 introduces a Background section and a separate theory section, moves Related Work after theory, reorganizes the appendices, and replaces numbered scenario classes with descriptive state categories. The contribution list and author block are also revised.

P2.justification: V3 changes the main text and references to two columns, redraws the graph-representation and inference diagrams, and replaces NBA posterior panels with court overlays. It adds GRN and NBA interaction visualizations, removes the earlier overview and linear-result tables, and relocates retained spring analyses to the appendix. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V3 substantially strengthens investigation of the central hidden-state problem: v2 supplied recurrent states, whereas v3 specifies and evaluates latent recurrent inference and uses controls that expose its remaining difficulties. Stronger comparator coverage, GRN evaluation and fuller implementation details make the method more assessable. The expanded theoretical framework states structural guarantees and limitations explicitly. These gains outweigh the loss of linear ablations and NBA transfer/data-efficiency evidence, although statistical reporting remains limited.
